***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on aviation]]
****[[Korean Air]] announces that it will acquire [[Asiana Airlines]] for 1.8 trillion [[South Korean won|KRW]] ([[US$]]1.6 billion) to help the [[South Korea]]n [[airline industry]] continue to grow amid uncertainties during the COVID-19 [[pandemic]]. ;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Iota]] strengthens into a [[Saffir–Simpson scale#Category 5|category 5]] hurricane as it approaches [[Nicaragua]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/weather/2020/11/16/iota-nicaragua-honduras-category-five/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[List of explosions]]
**An [[LP gas]] [[Tank truck|truck]] explodes on [[Mexican Federal Highway 15D|Federal Highway 15D]] in [[Nayarit]], [[Mexico]], killing at least 14 people. Most of the victims died inside their vehicles. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/gas-explosion-nayarit-mexico-b1723943.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/estados/explosion-de-pipa-en-la-autopista-tepic-guadalajara-suma-13-muertes (''El Universal'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania]]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Philadelphia]]
******[[Philadelphia]] bans nearly all indoor gatherings, both public and private, between November 20 and January 1 as part of new restrictions in the wake of a spike in COVID-19 cases. In addition, high schools will be reverted to remote learning, restaurants will only be allowed to have takeaway or delivery, and businesses like movie theaters, arcades, and bowling alleys are ordered closed again. [https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/11/16/935584213/philadelphia-bans-nearly-all-indoor-gatherings-for-the-rest-of-the-year (NPR)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[Governor of California|Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] announces that he has pulled an "emergency brake", which means that starting the following day, [[California]] will implement more closures and stricter restrictions, which will cover 41 counties containing 94% of the state's population. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/16/california-coronavirus-surge-roll-back-reopening (''The Guardian'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
*****[[Michigan]] surpasses 8,000 confirmed deaths from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2020/11/michigan-surpasses-8k-coronavirus-deaths.html (MLive.com)] 
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico]]
*****[[New Mexico]] begins its two-week lockdown announced by [[Governor of New Mexico|Governor]] [[Michelle Lujan Grisham]] on November 13 in an attempt to curb COVID-19 infections. Under the latest public health order, people are being asked to stay at home, and only essential businesses will remain open. [https://www.kob.com/albuquerque-news/new-mexico-begins-lockdown-as-state-looks-to-curb-spread/5926055/ (KOB-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
*****[[Texas]] surpasses 20,000 total confirmed deaths from COVID-19 and becomes the state with the second-highest number of reported deaths in the [[United States]], behind only [[New York (state)|New York]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/texas-surpasses-20000-virus-deaths-highest-us-74236569 (ABC News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****[[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representatives]] [[Cheri Bustos]] of [[Illinois]] and [[Tim Walberg]] of Michigan announce they have tested positive for COVID-19. Additionally, Representative [[Mark Pocan]] of Wisconsin said publicly he was isolating after a possible exposure to the virus. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/16/politics/lawmakers-members-covid-19-congress/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta]]
*****[[Alberta]] reports a record 91 new fatalities in the last 24 hours. [https://www.airdrietoday.com/local-news/alberta-records-20-covid-19-deaths-in-24-hours-2885060 (Airdrie Today)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nunavut]]
*****Chief Medical Officer Dr. Michael Patterson announces that [[Nunavut]] will close all non-essential services, businesses and organizations, as well as schools and daycare centres for two weeks beginning November 18, due to a spike in COVID-19 cases in the territory. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/nunavut-premier-to-give-update-on-covid-19-outbreak-1.5803373 (CBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 22,778 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases to 1.95 million. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/russia-registers-new-record-number-of-covid-19-cases/2045382 (Anadolu Agency)]
****[[Buryatia]] becomes the first Russian [[Republics of Russia|republic]] to return to a [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]], as it closes restaurants, shopping malls, and other places of public gathering for two weeks. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/11/16/first-russian-region-returns-to-full-lockdown-as-coronavirus-surges-a72051 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The number of hospitalized patients in [[France]] reaches an all-time high of 33,497. [https://www.lefigaro.fr/flash-actu/covid-19-508-deces-a-l-hopital-en-24-heures-nouveau-record-d-hospitalisations-en-france-20201116 (''Le Figaro'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record 91 new fatalities, bringing the nationwide death toll to 3,472. [https://www.portugalresident.com/new-daily-death-toll-record-portugal-registers-91-covid-19-victims-and-3996-new-cases/ (Portugal Resident)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]]
****[[Prime Minister of Sweden|Prime Minister]] [[Stefan Löfven]] announces a ban on public gatherings of more than eight people beginning November 24, as part of measures aimed to curb the spread of COVID-19 in [[Sweden]]. [https://www.rte.ie/news/coronavirus/2020/1116/1178372-world-covid/ (RTE)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 13,053 new cases and 486 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases in the worst-hit country in the [[Middle East]] to 775,121 and the nationwide death toll to 41,979. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/coronavirus/2020/11/16/Coronavirus-Iran-registers-record-daily-rise-in-COVID-19-cases-deaths (Al Arabiya)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Prime Minister of Pakistan|Prime Minister]] [[Imran Khan]] announces a temporary ban on political rallies and gatherings of more than 300 people in an attempt to reduce the spread of [[COVID-19]] in [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.deccanherald.com/international/world-news-politics/pakistan-suspends-political-rallies-to-prevent-spread-of-coronavirus-916337.html (''Deccan Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***The [[Northern Territory]], [[Queensland]], and [[Tasmania]] announce that their borders with [[South Australia]] are indefinitely closed, as the [[states and territories of Australia|state]]'s second wave reaches 17 cases. [https://www.news.com.au/travel/travel-updates/health-safety/australian-borders-more-states-close-to-south-australia-as-outbreak-explodes/news-story/6a0f83097d5e0724ffa1ad3d3b124842 (News.com.au)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Moderna]]'s preliminary results show [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|their vaccine candidate]] is 94.5% effective at preventing COVID-19 infections. The results also suggest that in cases of COVID-19 infection after vaccination, the vaccine appeared to prevent severe illness. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/11/16/health/Covid-moderna-vaccine.html (''The New York Times'')]

;International relations
*[[Russia–Sudan relations]]
**[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] approves the construction of a new [[Russian Navy]] facility in [[Sudan]]. The [[naval base]] will be built near [[Port Sudan]] on the [[Red Sea]] coast, and will hold up to 300 [[Russian Armed Forces|military]] and civilian personnel. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-russia-sudan-navy/putin-extending-russian-footprint-approves-new-naval-facility-in-sudan-idUKKBN27W2W9 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Capital punishment in Iraq]]
**Iraq [[Hanging|hangs]] 21 convicted [[terrorist]]s and [[murder]]ers at the [[Nasiriyah Central Prison]] in [[Nasiriyah]], [[Dhi Qar Governorate]]. The [[Interior Ministry (Iraq)|interior ministry]] did not provide details of the crimes of those executed but stated they were all convicted under a 2005 [[counter-terrorism]] law. [https://www.dw.com/en/iraq-hangs-21-terrorism-convicts-in-latest-mass-executions/a-55620661 (DW)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 United States presidential election]]
**Plaintiffs aligned with [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s re-election campaign and the [[Republican Party (United States)|GOP]] announces that they will drop [[Post-election lawsuits related to the 2020 U.S. presidential election|lawsuits]] in [[Pennsylvania]], [[Wisconsin]], [[Michigan]], and [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] challenging ballots and attempting to block the states from certifying their election results. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2020/11/16/gop-suddenly-drops-election-lawsuits-in-four-battleground-states-pennsylvania-wisconsin-georgia-michigan-amid-recent-court-failures/?sh=846c77a42191 (Forbes)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/11/16/trump-backers-drop-biden-vote-challenge-case-in-wisconsin.html (CNBC)]
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**Retirees protest in [[Minsk]], marking the 100th straight day protests broke in [[Belarus]] since [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] won his 6th term in a widely rejected [[2020 Belarusian presidential election|election]]. [https://apnews.com/article/international-news-alexander-lukashenko-belarus-sviatlana-tsikhanouskaya-minsk-3ab21b13c8eaa67c6ce6a27aad9945ef (AP)]
